seen_animation: A rowboat drawn as a two-line hull (pointed left end, rounded right end) carries two small stick figures with round heads. It starts cut off at the left edge in frame 1 and travels steadily to the right across the lower-middle of the frame, getting larger as it goes, until its right end is cut off by the right edge in frames 15-16. A grey treeline and shore sit along the top, with grey wave squiggles on the water. Throughout, the two figures' paddles cycle through very different positions from frame to frame: crossed diagonally through the hull (1, 5, 9, 13), one paddle angled down and back behind the boat (2, 6, 10, 14), a tall triangle of paddle raised above the rear figure (3, 7, 11, 15), and one paddle sticking out flat to the left past the stern (4, 8, 12, 16).
seen_film: A long canoe with two paddlers enters at the left edge in frame 1 and moves steadily to the right across the lower-middle of the frame, growing larger as it approaches the camera, until its bow is cut off by the right edge in frames 15-16. A dark treeline and pale shoreline run along the top. Both paddlers stroke continuously on the near side: the stern paddler's paddle reaches back toward the water behind the canoe and the bow paddler's arms rise and fall. The paddles stay low, near the gunwale and the water. They never go straight up above the heads and never swing across the hull. A faint wake trails behind.
named_subject: A rowboat/canoe with two stick-figure paddlers moving left to right across a lake.
evidence: The boat's travel matches the film. In g.png the path runs evenly from left to right with no gaps or reversals. It enters cut off at the left in e.png frames 1-3, as the film does in f.png 1-3, and is cut off at the right in e.png 36-38, as in f.png 36-38. Its size grows at about the film's rate. The paddling does not match. In e.png the paddles jump to a new pose on every frame on a 5-frame loop. In frames 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 one paddle stands straight up above the front figure as a bold vertical stick. In frames 4, 9, 14, 19, 24, 29 and 34 a paddle forms a tall raised triangle. In frames 6, 11, 16, 21, 26 and 36 a paddle crosses diagonally through the hull and out below the keel. In frames 8, 13, 18, 22, 28, 33 and 38 a paddle points out flat past the stern. Each consecutive pair (for example 4->5->6, 19->20->21, 34->35->36) swings the paddle through 90-180 degrees and switches it between figures and between sides of the boat. In f.png the paddles stay low on the near side and change only a little between frames. The paddles are also drawn much longer than the boat's depth and reach far below the hull, and the film does not show this.
primary_gap: The paddles pop to an unrelated pose on every frame (straight up, crossed through the hull, flat out the back), so the stroke reads as flicker instead of the film's low, steady near-side paddling.
closes_when: Each paddle stays on the near side, stays below head height, and moves through a short back-and-down arc that changes by only a small angle between consecutive e.png frames, with no vertical-stick frames (5, 10, 15, ...) and no paddles crossing through the hull.
protect: Keep the hull drawn as in c.png (two-line hull, pointed left tip, rounded right end, thin wobbly stroke). Keep the even left-to-right path and the growth in size that match the film. Keep the entry cut off at the left edge and the exit cut off at the right edge at the film's frames. Keep the two small stick figures placed where the film's two paddlers sit, and keep the grey treeline and water scenery behind them.
identity_gap: The hull matches c.png's construction, but c.png's single paddle line, which crosses the hull diagonally, has become two over-long paddles that flail in every direction, and the doodle never draws them that way.
